name: false life
lore:
# False Life: The Borrowed Breath

To weave *False Life* is to touch the hem of the shroud. As the incantation leaves your lips, the Weave feels clammy and heavy, like damp wool pulled tight over the soul. It is not the warm thrum of true vitality, but a cold, tethered echo.

Visually, the magic manifests as a pallid, opalescent shimmer—a ghostly second skin that clings to the caster’s form. This "shroud" does not mend bone or knit flesh; rather, it acts as a spectral buffer, absorbing the kinetic cruelty of the world before it can reach your true essence.

Scholars trace its origin to the "Hollow King" Malakor. Trapped within a collapsing tomb, Malakor realized that if he could not find life, he would mimic its endurance. He stitched together the lingering miasma of the crypt to bolster his failing frame, walking out of the rubble as a man of living marble, though his heart remained silent. It is a grim comfort, adventurer, but in the dark, a borrowed breath is better than none.
